target.title: fix(matrix): cross-signing bootstrap dead-ends on MAS-fronted Synapse with misleading matrix.password error
target.body:
Closes #74504

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix bots that authenticate with a Personal Access Token against a Synapse homeserver fronted by Matrix Authentication Service (MSC3861 / MAS, the Element ESS default) could never publish cross-signing keys. `openclaw matrix verify bootstrap` and channel startup failed with the misleading error `Matrix cross-signing key upload requires UIA; provide matrix.password for m.login.password fallback`, even though the homeserver does not advertise `m.login.password` for that upload, the bot has no password on MAS, and setting one would not help. The bootstrap also blindly escalated to a fresh-identity reset upload that deterministically 401s on MAS, producing two confusing back-to-back failures, and the MAS recovery URL that Synapse includes in the 401 challenge was silently discarded. With cross-signing unpublished, E2EE decryption and self-verification stay broken for the deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The signing-key upload UIA callback in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/crypto-bootstrap.ts` retried hardcoded auth shapes (`null`, `m.login.dummy`, `m.login.password`) without ever inspecting the 401 challenge body, and omitted the UIA `session` token that the spec expects follow-up attempts to carry. The fix makes the callback route by what the homeserver actually advertises: `m.login.dummy` and `m.login.password` are attempted only when offered (now with the session token threaded through), the MAS interactive reset stage (`org.matrix.cross_signing_reset`, or its newer `m.oauth` form) becomes a typed `MatrixCrossSigningResetRequiredError` carrying the reset URL from the challenge `params`, non-UIA failures are rethrown unchanged, and other unsatisfiable stage sets get a `MatrixUiaUnsupportedStagesError` naming the stages. Cross-signing bootstrap stops escalating to `setupNewCrossSigning` retries once interactive approval is required and logs the actionable URL once instead.

Two deliberate boundaries: the first upload attempt stays unauthenticated, so the MSC3967 first-publish path and uploads inside a fresh MAS approval window keep succeeding through the same code path (the upload attempt itself is the only reliable probe for whether the operator's browser approval is still current). And the fix reads the reset URL from the 401 challenge that Synapse already sends rather than adding a homeserver capability probe, keeping the change local to the UIA callback that owns challenge handling; when a homeserver advertises the reset stage without a URL, the error directs the operator to homeserver admin tooling.

## User Impact

Operators of bots on MAS-fronted homeservers now get one actionable failure instead of a dead end: the bootstrap error names the MAS cross-signing reset URL to open in a browser, and re-running the bootstrap within the approval window publishes cross-signing through the normal path. Fresh bots on MAS publish their first identity without any interactive step via MSC3967. Deployments using `m.login.dummy` or a configured `matrix.password` keep working, now with the UIA session token attached as the spec requires. Operators without a configured password on non-MAS homeservers that require `m.login.password` see an error naming the actual missing configuration instead of a generic UIA message.

## Evidence

Reproduced by driving the real production runtime: the plugin's `MatrixClient` (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts`) with the real rust crypto stack (`matrix-sdk-crypto-wasm` via `matrix-js-sdk`), real SQLite-backed plugin state, and the real `bootstrapOwnDeviceVerification()` entry point that `openclaw matrix verify bootstrap` calls. The only substituted seam is the homeserver itself: a local HTTP server replaying the exact 401 challenge that MAS-fronted Synapse returns on `/keys/device_signing/upload` (per Synapse's MSC3861 implementation, element-hq/synapse#17509). Identical driver and inputs for all runs.

Before, on pristine `main` (`2f00a417edde`, Matrix surface identical to current `main`): four 401 upload attempts across the initial pass and the blind reset escalation, the misleading `matrix.password` hint, and no reset URL surfaced anywhere:

```
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:42409/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [11ms 401]
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:42409/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [12ms 401]
[MatrixClientLite] Initial cross-signing bootstrap failed, trying reset: Error: Matrix cross-signing key upload requires UIA; provide matrix.password for m.login.password fallback
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:42409/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [9ms 401]
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:42409/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [12ms 401]
[MatrixClientLite] Failed to bootstrap cross-signing: Error: Matrix cross-signing key upload requires UIA; provide matrix.password for m.login.password fallback
Bootstrap success: no
Bootstrap error: Matrix cross-signing key upload requires UIA; provide matrix.password for m.login.password fallback
Cross-signing published: no
```

After, this patch, identical inputs: a single upload attempt and a typed error carrying the MAS reset URL from the challenge (the token is elided by the existing log sanitizer):

```
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:32883/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [10ms 401]
[MatrixClientLite] Cross-signing bootstrap needs interactive approval: Matrix cross-signing key upload requires interactive approval from the homeserver auth service. Open https://mas.example.org/account/cross_signing_reset?token=redact…oken in a browser as the bot user, approve the cross-signing reset, then re-run the bootstrap while the approval is fresh.
Bootstrap success: no
Bootstrap error: Matrix cross-signing key upload requires interactive approval from the homeserver auth service. Open https://mas.example.org/account/cross_signing_reset?token=redact…oken in a browser as the bot user, approve the cross-signing reset, then re-run the bootstrap while the approval is fresh.
Cross-signing published: no
```

After, this patch, with the server accepting the unauthenticated upload (the MSC3967 first-publish case, and equally the state after the operator approves the reset in MAS): the same code path publishes cross-signing:

```
[MatrixClient] FetchHttpApi: <-- POST http://127.0.0.1:45899/_matrix/client/v3/keys/device_signing/upload [11ms 200]
[MatrixClientLite] Cross-signing bootstrap complete
Cross-signing published: yes
```

Validation on the changed files:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/` passes (12 files, 121 tests). The 7 new or updated regression tests in `crypto-bootstrap.test.ts` fail on pristine `main` and pass with this patch: stage routing with session threading for dummy and password, the typed MAS reset error with URL for both `org.matrix.cross_signing_reset` and `m.oauth`, no fresh-identity retry after the reset stage rejects an upload, the reset upload still being attempted after an import-key mismatch so a fresh MAS approval can land, non-UIA errors rethrown unchanged, and the MSC3967 no-auth first upload.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and the `tsgo` extensions and extensions-test lanes are clean on the changed files.

Not tested: no live MAS-fronted Synapse deployment was driven; the homeserver HTTP responses were emulated at the network seam from the challenge shape documented in #74504 and Synapse's implementation. No full build was run (no module boundaries or packaging touched).
